Hi Samir / Ava —

Great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps on the integration side so the engineering teams can plan: 

Summary of asks we heard:
- Private connectivity: you want Redwood traffic to originate from VPC endpoints in your AWS account and to restrict inbound connections to a small set of IPs (IP allowlist).
- Egress / DNS: FinPay needs egress through your NAT + DNS resolution inside the VPC (no public DNS leaks).
- Mutual TLS: mTLS for authenticated calls from FinPay services to Redwood (client certs).
- Embeddings/reranker: you'll be calling embeddings and a reranker pipeline; expect batched requests and streaming for generation.

What our team will provide:
- Concrete IP ranges (we can provide stable egress IPs for Dedicated / Private).
- A short integration guide (SDK auth flows, required headers, example TLS client config) — attaching the integration guide and the network checklist.
- Suggested routing: direct VPC endpoint + allowlist + DNS override for redwood-internal domains to resolve to the private endpoint.

Next steps / owners:
1) We (Redwood) send a short network checklist + egress IPs (Jonas) — by end of day tomorrow.
2) FinPay to share firewall rules / current NAT egress config (Samir) and the internal DNS zone names that need to resolve privately.
3) Schedule a technical working session (30–45m) to walk through the mTLS cert exchange and SDK auth (propose Fri 6/12 10:00 PT).

Attachments: finpay-network-requirements.xlsx (your sheet) — I captured a few items during the call and added a column for answers.

If anything above is off, flag it here and I’ll adjust. Otherwise I’ll schedule the working session and Jonas will include the IP ranges + integration guide.

Hi Samir / team —

Short answers up front: we support both options (VPC Endpoint / PrivateLink in customer account OR stable egress IPs from Dedicated). Which is best depends on your security posture and whether you want inbound-only VPC endpoints or outbound-only allowlist control. 

Details / implementation notes:
- Option A (Preferred for max isolation): AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service) — we can publish a service in our account and you create an interface endpoint in yours. Pros: private traffic, no public IPs. Cons: needs cross-account endpoint acceptance and ENI limits.
- Option B (Simpler for short pilots): Allowlist Redwood egress IP ranges. We can allocate a small set of stable IPs from our Dedicated fleet for your account; these are the ones we use for egress and will be in the integration guide.

IP / port requirements (typical):
- Outbound from FinPay to Redwood: TCP 443 (HTTPS) to the PrivateLink endpoint or to listed egress IPs.
- DNS: If using PrivateLink, create a private hosted zone mapping redwood-internal.example -> endpoint IPs (we’ll provide the FQNs).
- mTLS: We support mutual TLS with client certs. FinPay can either: 
   1) Upload client certs to our portal (short-term), or
   2) Integrate with your internal cert manager and rotate certs; we accept cert bundles via S3 with an IAM role we request for initial bootstrap.

Auth / SDK notes:
- SDKs support API key + optional mTLS. When mTLS is enabled we will enforce client cert validation and still require the API key for routing/billing.
- For embeddings/reranking: enable batching in the SDK (batch size and flush interval configurable). For 50 req/s pilot, start with batch size 8 and max latency target 250ms. We’ll help tune after the pilot.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-integration-guide.pdf (contains IP list, example security group rules, DNS entries, and mTLS cert upload flow).

I’ll be on the working session Friday and can walk through the PrivateLink flow and cert exchange.

— Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
